clauses.reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12257, whose subject line describes noncompetitive conversion of CETA participants to career or career-conditional civil service status. Sections 1-101 to 1-106 let Executive agencies, with the approval of the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, give excepted appointments up to grade GS-3 to persons who completed Comprehensive Employment and Training Act job training or a hosted work experience program within three months, allow noncompetitive conversion to career or career-conditional appointment after six months of satisfactory service, and direct the Director to issue guidelines and regulations. No earlier express end was found.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12257 (45 FR 84005, Federal Register of December 22, 1980; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Noncompetitive Conversion of CETA Participants to Career or Career-Conditional Civil Service Status and signed December 18, 1980. It authorizes noncompetitive appointment and conversion of former CETA participants to the civil service. Inventory: six numbered sections (1-101 to 1-106) that form one appointment-and-conversion authority, recorded as one whole clause. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12257, whose subject line describes noncompetitive conversion of CETA participants to career or career-conditional civil service status. The order has no sunset, fixed date or report clause. The Comprehensive Employment and Training Act is not held; its expiry is an unnamed instrument and a disclosed candidate only (owner ruling 2026-10-21, unnamed instruments).  The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found no held text citing this order by number other than its own printings. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).
